title: When Attribution Patching Lies: Diagnosis and a Second-Order Correction
abstract: arXiv:2606.09899v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: A central goal of mechanistic interpretability is to identify which internal components causally drive a language model's behavior. Because these importance estimates serve as the evidence for identifying circuits, systematic errors can lead to the misidentification of the underlying mechanisms. While activation patching provides a gold-standard causal metric, its computational cost is prohibitive at scale. Practitioners instead rely on attribution patching, a gradient-based, first-order approximation whose reliability remains poorly understood. In this work, we characterize the source of this unreliability, demonstrating that the dominant error stems from the non-linearities in the downstream network rather than local curvature at the patched component. translated_title: 当归因修补失效时：诊断与二阶修正
translated_abstract: 机械可解释性的一个核心目标是识别哪些内部组件因果地驱动语言模型的行为。由于这些重要性估计是识别电路的证据基础，系统性的误差可能导致对底层机制的错误识别。虽然激活修补提供了黄金标准的因果度量，但其计算成本在大规模应用时过于高昂。因此，实践者转而依赖归因修补，这是一种基于梯度的一阶近似方法，但其可靠性仍缺乏充分理解。在这项工作中，我们刻画了这种不可靠性的来源，证明其主要误差源于下游网络中的非线性，而非被修补组件处的局部曲率。这一洞见带来了三个实用工具：（i）一个用于检测不可信估计的可靠性分数；（ii）量化潜在归因错误设定的误差界限；（（摘要此处截断，第三项工具应为标题中提到的二阶修正）
tldr: 本文揭示归因修补的主要误差源于下游网络的非线性而非被修补组件的局部曲率，并据此提出可靠性分数、误差界限与二阶修正三项工具来诊断和改进归因修补的可信度。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that attribution patching's dominant errors stem from non-linearities in the downstream network rather than local curvature at the patched component, and introduces three practical tools—a reliability score, error bounds, and a second-order correction—to diagnose and improve the trustworthiness of attribution patching.
